scenes.dialogue: Ravi and Mohan settle after a neighbourhood fight. In another case, Rohan wants to accept responsibility.
He wants a lawful reduction in punishment. Are these the same thing?
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or B N S S, these are two different procedures: compounding and plea bargaining.
scenes.shown: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or BNSS, these are two different procedures: compounding and plea bargaining.

scenes.dialogue: One can have the effect of an acquittal. The other is supervised by the court, and may end in conviction with a reduced sentence.
Section Three Fifty Nine lists the offences that can be compounded, and who may compound each one. The person named in the table must agree.
scenes.shown: Section 359 lists the offences that can be compounded, and who may compound each one. The person named in the table must agree.

scenes.dialogue: Suppose Ravi causes Mohan simple hurt, charged only under B N S Section One Fifteen, sub section Two.
scenes.shown: Suppose Ravi causes Mohan simple hurt, charged only under BNS Section 115(2).

scenes.dialogue: The first table lets Mohan, the injured person, compound that offence without the court's permission needed for the second table.
The compromise must still be placed before the court. It is a legal process, not merely a handshake.
Now change the example. Ravi is charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt under B N S Section One Seventeen, sub section Two.
scenes.shown: Now change the example. Ravi is charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt under BNS Section 117(2).

scenes.dialogue: That offence appears in the second table, so Mohan's agreement also needs the court's permission.
Section Three Fifty Nine, sub section Eight, says lawful compounding has the effect of an acquittal of the accused concerned.
scenes.shown: Section 359(8) says lawful compounding has the effect of an acquittal of the accused concerned.

scenes.dialogue: Simple and grievous hurt have different compounding requirements. Always check the exact charge.
Section Three Fifty Nine sets no general thirty day or sixty day deadline for compounding. But the stage of the case matters.
scenes.shown: Section 359 sets no general 30-day or 60-day deadline for compounding. But the stage of the case matters.

scenes.dialogue: After commitment for trial, or during an appeal after conviction, the court's leave is required under sub section Five.
scenes.shown: After commitment for trial, or during an appeal after conviction, the court's leave is required under sub-section (5).

scenes.dialogue: A private settlement cannot make every offence compoundable. Murder, for example, cannot be compounded under this section.
Special statutes can have their own rules. Before promising a compromise will end a case, check every charge and the necessary court process.
Plea bargaining has a separate eligibility test under Section Two Eighty Nine.
scenes.shown: Plea bargaining has a separate eligibility test under Section 289.

scenes.dialogue: It excludes offences punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment exceeding seven years.
It also excludes offences against women or children, and notified offences affecting the country's socio economic condition.
scenes.shown: It also excludes offences against women or children, and notified offences affecting the country's socio-economic condition.

scenes.dialogue: Section Three Hundred excludes juvenile or child accused from this chapter.
scenes.shown: Section 300 excludes juvenile or child accused from this chapter.

scenes.dialogue: An earlier conviction for the same offence is another obstacle, under Section Two Ninety.
scenes.shown: An earlier conviction for the same offence is another obstacle, under Section 290.

scenes.dialogue: So Rohan must qualify before any talk of compensation or punishment can begin.
Assume Rohan is an adult accused in an eligible property case.
Under Section Two Ninety, sub section One, he can apply to the trial court within thirty days from framing of the charge.
scenes.shown: Under Section 290(1), he can apply to the trial court within 30 days from framing of the charge.

scenes.dialogue: The application briefly describes the case, and includes his sworn affidavit.
It confirms that he acts voluntarily, understands the punishment, and has no previous conviction for the same offence.
The clock is tied to framing the charge. It does not begin simply because the F I R was registered or Rohan was arrested.
scenes.shown: The clock is tied to framing the charge. It does not begin simply because the FIR was registered or Rohan was arrested.

scenes.dialogue: The judge examines Rohan privately, with the other party absent, to check that his application is voluntary.
If satisfied, Section Two Ninety, sub section Four, requires the court to give the parties time, not exceeding sixty days.
scenes.shown: If satisfied, Section 290(4) requires the court to give the parties time, not exceeding 60 days.

scenes.dialogue: That time is to work out a mutually satisfactory disposition, which may include compensation and expenses for the victim.
This is a separate period, allowed by the court. It is not sixty days from arrest.
scenes.shown: This is a separate period, allowed by the court. It is not 60 days from arrest.

scenes.dialogue: And it does not guarantee that the whole case finishes within ninety days.
scenes.shown: And it does not guarantee that the whole case finishes within 90 days.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Ninety One brings the participants into a voluntary process.
scenes.shown: Section 291 brings the participants into a voluntary process.

scenes.dialogue: In a police report case, these include the prosecutor, the investigating officer, the accused and the victim.
Section Two Ninety Two requires a signed report if agreement is reached. If not, proceedings resume from the application stage.
scenes.shown: Section 292 requires a signed report if agreement is reached. If not, proceedings resume from the application stage.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Ninety Nine protects statements or facts in the application from being used for other purposes.
scenes.shown: Section 299 protects statements or facts in the application from being used for other purposes.

scenes.dialogue: Rohan cannot be forced to agree. And filing alone does not complete the process.
Section Two Ninety Three provides for victim compensation, and for probation where applicable.
scenes.shown: Section 293 provides for victim compensation, and for probation where applicable.

scenes.dialogue: It also sets reduced sentences. Take an eligible offence with no minimum sentence, and an accused never previously convicted.
The court may impose one sixth of the punishment provided or extendable. If the maximum is three years, that fraction is six months.
scenes.shown: The court may impose one-sixth of the punishment provided or extendable. If the maximum is three years, that fraction is six months.

scenes.dialogue: Where a statutory minimum applies, the first time offender fraction is one fourth of that minimum.
scenes.shown: Where a statutory minimum applies, the first-time offender fraction is one-fourth of that minimum.

scenes.dialogue: These are conditional court decisions, not a guaranteed discount negotiated privately.
Under Section Two Ninety Four, the plea bargaining judgment is delivered in open court.
scenes.shown: Under Section 294, the plea bargaining judgment is delivered in open court.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Ninety Five makes it final, with no ordinary appeal, while preserving the specified constitutional remedies.
scenes.shown: Section 295 makes it final, with no ordinary appeal, while preserving the specified constitutional remedies.

scenes.dialogue: Remember the difference. Lawful compounding has the effect of acquittal.
Plea bargaining can result in conviction, with a lawful sentencing benefit.
Check eligibility, get independent legal advice, and understand the consequences before agreeing.
Neither an informal compromise nor an application alone can replace the required legal process.
